:::{#exm-surprisal-coin}
#### Surprisal of the values of a biased coin flip

Let $X$ be $1$ if one flip of a coin lands heads and $0$ if it lands tails, with $\P(X=1) = \tfrac{1}{4}$ and $\P(X=0) = \tfrac{3}{4}$.
Using logarithms to base 2, so that [surprisal](#def-surprisal) is measured in bits, the surprisal of heads is $\surprisalf{1} = -\log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} = 2$ bits,
and the surprisal of tails is $\surprisalf{0} = -\log_2 \tfrac{3}{4} = \log_2 \tfrac{4}{3} \approx 0.415$ bits.
For a fair coin, each value of $X$ has surprisal $-\log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} = 1$ bit.

:::
